p: not thou silence: This psalm seems to have been composed as a form of prayer against the dangers that the Church was in, in the days of Jehoshaphat.
enemies make a tumult: He calls them God's enemies, who are enemies of his Church.
hidden ones: The elect of God are his secret ones: for he hides them in the secret of his tabernacle, and preserves them from all dangers.
cut them off from being a: They were not content to take the Church as prisoner: but sought to utterly destroy it.
with one consent: By all secret means.
against thee: They thought to have subverted your counsel in which the constancy of the Church was established.
of Lot: The wickedness of the Ammonites and Moabites is described in that they provoked these other nations to fight against the Israelites.
Midianites: By these examples they were confirmed that God would not permit his people to be completely destroyed, Jud 7:21,4:15.
dung for the earth: Trodden under foot as mire.
houses of God in possession: That is, Judea: for where his Church is, there he dwells among them.
wheel: Because the reprobate could by no means be amended, he prays that they may utterly be destroyed, be unstable and led by all winds.
seek thy name: That is, be compelled by your plagues to confess your power.
know that thou: Though they do not believe, yet they may prove by experience, that it is in vain to resist against your counsel in establishing your Church.
